issues.title: Sinestro, Part One
issues.summary: On Oa, the Guardians allow Sinestro to wield a Green Lantern ring again, despite Ganthet’s doubts. Meanwhile, Hal Jordan is stranded on Earth without his ring and struggles to keep his life together. After a misunderstanding involving Carol Ferris, he returns home to find an eviction notice. On Korugar, Sinestro discovers that the Sinestro Corps has enslaved the people he once ruled. He kills a disobedient Corps member and destroys the soldier’s yellow ring. Realizing his former followers have become a threat to his homeworld, Sinestro travels to Earth and finds Hal. He offers to restore Hal’s ring—but only if Hal agrees to follow his orders.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Two
issues.summary: Sinestro offers Hal Jordan a new Green Lantern ring, but Hal attacks him as soon as he puts it on. Sinestro reveals that he can control the ring and shut it down whenever he chooses, making Hal dependent on him. When a bridge collapses in Coast City, Hal tries to save the victims, but Sinestro disables his ring to teach him a lesson. Sinestro then rescues everyone and reconstructs the bridge, demonstrating a more effective use of the ring. Their demonstration is interrupted by Gorgor, a Sinestro Corps member responsible for the disaster. Sinestro kills him and explains that his Corps has become cruel and tyrannical. He needs Hal's help to free Korugar from his own former army.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Three
issues.summary: Hal agrees to accompany Sinestro to Korugar, though he refuses to accept Sinestro's claim of superiority. On Oa, the Guardians strip Ganthet of his emotions and discuss replacing the Green Lantern Corps with a new force. Meanwhile, Hal and Sinestro arrive on Korugar and plan to disable the Sinestro Corps' Central Power Battery. Sinestro draws the Corps members away while Hal enters the battery, but it begins to disintegrate him. As Sinestro watches in horror, the mission appears to have ended in disaster. On Earth, Carol Ferris sees news footage of Hal working alongside Sinestro and cannot believe they have become allies.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Four
issues.summary: Hal is seemingly disintegrated inside the Sinestro Corps' Central Power Battery, while Sinestro struggles to understand what has happened. The battery's reaction to the Green Lantern energy destabilizes it, and Hal eventually emerges alive, though badly shaken. Sinestro's attempt to liberate Korugar grows more complicated as the enslaved Korugarians remain afraid of him because of his own history as their ruler. Arsona and other prisoners resist the Corps, while Sinestro confronts the consequences of the army he created. The pair must find a way to defeat the Corps and its power source before the people of Korugar can truly be free.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Five
issues.summary: Hal and Sinestro continue their fight to free Korugar from the Sinestro Corps. The imprisoned Korugarians obtain temporary power rings and try to turn them against Sinestro, but the rings cannot harm their creator. Professor Insidd attempts to find a way to neutralize Sinestro's power battery, only for the battery to respond to Sinestro's commands and kill him. The resistance faces the danger of becoming consumed by revenge, while Sinestro must confront the consequences of the Corps' rule and his own legacy. Hal and Sinestro push toward a final confrontation with the force that has enslaved Korugar.

issues.title: The Other Hero
issues.summary: With the battle for Korugar over, Sinestro and Hal face the question of what comes next. Sinestro sends Hal back to Earth, where Hal tries to repair his damaged relationship with Carol Ferris and acknowledge the mistakes he has made. Their partnership has shown Hal a different, more ruthless kind of heroism, even as Sinestro remains a deeply troubling ally. On Oa, the Guardians pursue a far more ominous plan: they intend to unleash the First Lantern and build a Third Army to replace the Green Lantern Corps. The victory on Korugar therefore closes one conflict while setting up a much larger threat to the universe.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part One
issues.summary:
Sinestro tries to make Hal Jordan work with him again, explaining that the Guardians intend to replace the Green Lantern Corps with a new force. Hal refuses to trust him, and their argument turns violent. When Indigo-1 and her Lanterns arrive, they seize Sinestro because they believe the Guardians made a mistake by giving him a green ring. Hal follows them to the Indigo homeworld rather than leave Sinestro in their hands.

On Oa, the Guardians interrogate Lyssa Drak about the Book of the Black and the First Lantern, revealing that they are pursuing their own secret plan. On the Indigo world, Hal wakes in a cell with his ring drained and encounters Black Hand, who has also been captured by the Tribe. Indigo-1’s intervention is not a rescue: she intends to deal with Sinestro herself.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part Two
issues.summary:
Hal and Sinestro are trapped on the Indigo homeworld, powerless and pursued by the Indigo Tribe. Sinestro is restrained and subjected to the Tribe’s influence, while Hal tries to understand why Indigo-1 has singled out his former mentor, Abin Sur. Their escape attempt forces Hal and Sinestro to cooperate even though neither trusts the other.

The issue explains that the Indigo Lanterns’ apparent compassion has a brutal origin: their power can suppress their former personalities and force them to feel empathy. Indigo-1’s connection to Abin Sur is central to the Tribe’s creation, and the story begins to reveal how he and Natromo turned violent criminals into Indigo Lanterns.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part Three
issues.summary:
Hal and Sinestro learn how the Indigo Tribe was created. Abin Sur and Natromo discovered the indigo light and used it to transform Iroque—a ruthless killer who would become Indigo-1—and other criminals into members of a group compelled to feel compassion. The Tribe’s benevolent appearance therefore hides a coercive form of rehabilitation: its members’ cruelty has been suppressed rather than simply overcome.

On Oa, the Guardians continue their own plan to replace the Green Lantern Corps, showing that they are willing to sacrifice their existing Lanterns to achieve it. The two storylines bring the series’ personal conflict over Sinestro together with the Guardians’ larger conspiracy.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part Four
issues.summary:
The origin of the Indigo Tribe is fully exposed: Abin Sur and Natromo created the Tribe to use the indigo light to force dangerous criminals to experience compassion. Indigo-1 was once Iroque, a killer whose personality was changed by the ring. The revelation explains why the Tribe has such a strong interest in Sinestro, whose own history makes him a candidate for the same forced transformation.

Hal and Sinestro’s encounter with the Tribe reaches its conclusion, but their problems are far from over. The Guardians continue preparing to replace the Green Lantern Corps, and their secret plans become the next major threat to Hal, Sinestro and the other Lanterns.

issues.title: The Revenge of Black Hand, Part One
issues.summary:
The Indigo Tribe releases Sinestro from its control and places him in Hal Jordan’s custody. Natromo has reversed the connection between their rings: Hal can now control Sinestro’s ring, just as Sinestro previously controlled Hal’s. Sinestro asks what happened to Black Hand, but the pair find only black residue near a cliff and realize that Black Hand has apparently killed himself to escape being taken by the Indigo Tribe again.

Black Hand has in fact returned from the dead. On Earth, he murders the people in a restaurant, then resurrects his own dead family in a cemetery. He announces his intention to turn everyone in the world into a zombie so that he will no longer be the only person separated from the living. Meanwhile, the Guardians locate Sinestro and begin closing in on him.

issues.title: The Revenge of Black Hand, Part Two
issues.summary:
Black Hand begins carrying out his plan to spread undeath. After escaping the Indigo Tribe by dying and returning to life, he resurrects his family and sets out to turn the living into zombies. His actions are not simply an attack on Hal Jordan: he wants to remake the world so that no one will be alive in the way that once made him feel isolated.

Hal and Sinestro are forced to pursue him while dealing with their reversed ring bond, which leaves Hal able to shut down Sinestro’s power. Indigo-1 and Natromo prepare the Tribe to confront the Guardians, believing that even the Guardians can be redeemed; Sinestro rejects that faith and warns Indigo-1 not to try to force him back into the Tribe. The conflict with Black Hand escalates toward the major turning point in Green Lantern Annual #1, which concludes this storyline.
